notes: Generalisation check for the category theory that survived the description-shape
experiment: process skills -- ones telling the agent HOW to work -- do not
auto-trigger regardless of wording. See docs/notes/skill-evals.md section 5.
test-driven-development is the clean test. Its description is process-shaped and
79 characters, structurally the same as writing-plans' 84-character precondition,
but it sits in the testing group rather than workflow, so it is not the same
sample that produced the theory.
Prediction, recorded before running: 0/8, matching the five silent workflow
skills. A non-zero result confines the theory to claude/workflow and means
something else is going on.
The near-miss arm is mostly other members of the testing group -- an anti-pattern
question belongs to testing-anti-patterns, a flaky-async question to
condition-based-waiting.
MATCHED PAIRS. The first run scored 1/8, and the single case that fired was the
only one asking for guidance -- 'How should I start?' -- while all seven silent
ones were imperatives: Implement, Add, Fix, Write, Build. That suggests the
determinant is the user's phrasing, not the skill's description, which would also
explain why the 2x2 description experiment was null in all four cells.
The last seven entries are those same seven tasks reframed as requests for
guidance. Same underlying work, different framing, so the pair isolates phrasing.
Prediction: the guidance-shaped seven fire and the imperative seven stay silent.
